title: Late-Pregnancy Tests: Lung Maturity, Fetal Fibronectin and MCA Doppler
summary: Learn what the L/S ratio, cervicovaginal fetal fibronectin and middle cerebral artery Doppler each measure, why gestational age outweighs a lung maturity result, why a negative fFN is the useful one, and what an MCA velocity above 1.5 MoM does and does not detect.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 26 Hit 8 (fetal lung maturity), Hit 9 (fetal fibronectin), Hit 11 (MCA Doppler for fetal anaemia), Exam Trap 5 (L/S at 30 weeks) and Exam Trap 6 (positive fFN), checked against Peppiatt 2024, St Clair 2008 (read via a page-fetch tool), Wijnberger 2010, Vanderhoeven 2014, Cao 2020, Ikeoha 2022, Chen 2012, Mahomed 2019, Peterson 2014, Di Renzo 2011, Brennand 2009 and Pasman 2015. Hit 8’s “don’t deliver <39 weeks without confirming unless dates are certain” presents a mature FLM test as licence for earlier delivery; Vanderhoeven 2014 found substantial morbidity before 39 weeks despite mature results and Peppiatt 2024 reports testing declined under stricter ACOG/NICHD indications (register flag rv-flm-mature-before-39-weeks). Hit 11’s “detects all fetal anemia” is qualified: Mari 2000 (via Brennand 2009) found 100% sensitivity for moderate or severe anaemia but no prediction of mild anaemia (register flag rv-mca-psv-moderate-severe-only). The reviewer’s fFN window “24–35 weeks” is taught as the sources’ 24–34 weeks. Not verified and not taught: PG “appears after ~35 weeks” and the reviewer’s hard “not useful before 32 weeks” cutoff (taught instead as gestational-age-dependent risk). The StatPearls L/S chapter (NCBI Bookshelf) was blocked by a browser verification page and was not read; the ACOG committee opinion itself was not read. Not taught: preeclampsia, Queenan curve, lamellar body count thresholds beyond the explanation.

objectives: State what the L/S ratio, phosphatidylglycerol, fetal fibronectin and MCA peak systolic velocity each measure.
Explain why gestational age outweighs a lung maturity result and why a mature result before 39 weeks does not guarantee a well neonate.
Interpret fFN (negative vs positive, valid sample) and an MCA PSV above 1.5 MoM, including what it does not detect.

scenes.title: Three late-pregnancy requests
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests arrive from the obstetric unit. (1) 30 weeks, a scheduled delivery is planned, and amniotic fluid is sent for an L/S ratio. (2) 29 weeks, contractions, intact membranes: cervicovaginal fetal fibronectin (fFN) is positive. (3) 28 weeks, anti-D alloimmunisation: middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA PSV) is 1.7 MoM. Question token: “Which result changes management?”

cues.text: Three requests from the obstetric unit. At thirty weeks, a delivery is being planned, and amniotic fluid arrives for a lecithin to sphingomyelin ratio.
At twenty-nine weeks, a woman with contractions has a positive fetal fibronectin. At twenty-eight weeks, an alloimmunised fetus has a fast middle cerebral artery flow.
Which of these results should change what happens next, and which is being over-read?

scenes.title: What each test measures
scenes.altText: Three schematic cards. Lungs: surfactant is mostly lecithin (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine); sphingomyelin exceeds lecithin until about 26 weeks, then lecithin rises; an L/S ratio of 2.0 (2:1) is the classic mature cutoff; L/S is affected by blood or meconium, while phosphatidylglycerol (PG) assays are not. Leak: fetal fibronectin is a glycoprotein of the choriodecidual interface; it is present in cervicovaginal fluid early in pregnancy, falls between 24 and 34 weeks, and reappears when the chorion separates from the decidua. Velocity: an anaemic fetus has a hyperdynamic circulation and thinner blood, so MCA peak systolic velocity rises. Token: MoM = measured value ÷ expected value for gestational age.

cues.text: Lungs first. Surfactant is mostly lecithin. Sphingomyelin outweighs lecithin until about twenty-six weeks; when lecithin is twice sphingomyelin, a ratio of two, the lung is classically called mature. Blood or meconium can distort the ratio, but phosphatidylglycerol assays are not affected.

Fetal fibronectin is a glycoprotein at the junction of the fetal membranes and the uterine lining. It is found in vaginal fluid early in pregnancy, normally fades between twenty-four and thirty-four weeks, and leaks again when that junction is disrupted.
The middle cerebral artery reports anaemia. An anaemic fetus pumps more blood, and its blood is thinner, so the peak systolic velocity in the brain artery rises.
Velocity changes with gestational age, so it is reported as a multiple of the median: the measured value divided by the value expected for that week.

props.label: MoM = measured ÷ expected for gestational age

scenes.title: The calendar beats the ratio; Doppler beats the needle
scenes.altText: Left card: in one cohort model (St Clair 2008), no L/S value brought the predicted risk of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) to 3% or less below 34 weeks, and at 26 weeks the risk was 97–99% whatever the L/S; neonates born before 39 weeks after a mature fetal lung maturity (FLM) result still had substantial morbidity (Vanderhoeven 2014); FLM testing has declined as stricter indications for late-preterm and early-term birth were adopted and antenatal corticosteroids became routine. Right card: amniotic fluid ΔOD450 (bilirubin) reflects haemolysis only, so it is less reliable in Kell disease, where erythroid suppression plays a large role; each amniocentesis carries a 0.25–1% loss rate and fetomaternal haemorrhage in 2.3–17%. Token: in the DIAMOND study, MCA Doppler detected severe anaemia with 88% sensitivity vs 76% for amniocentesis.

cues.text: For fetal lungs, gestational age outweighs the ratio. In one cohort model, no lecithin to sphingomyelin value brought the risk of respiratory distress down to three percent before thirty-four weeks, and at twenty-six weeks the risk stayed at ninety-seven to ninety-nine percent whatever the ratio.

And a mature result is not a mature baby. Neonates born before thirty-nine weeks after a mature lung test still had substantial morbidity. Testing has declined as stricter delivery-timing indications and routine antenatal steroids took over.

For fetal anaemia, the old method was amniocentesis to measure bilirubin by its absorbance at four hundred fifty nanometres. Bilirubin reflects haemolysis only, so it is less reliable in Kell disease, and every tap risks pregnancy loss and fetomaternal haemorrhage.
In the DIAMOND study, Doppler of the middle cerebral artery detected severe anaemia more often than amniocentesis: eighty-eight versus seventy-six percent. Doppler became the standard.

props.title: Calendar beats the ratio
lines: < 34 wk: no L/S gave ≤ 3% RDS risk

scenes.title: Reading fFN and MCA results
scenes.altText: fFN card: positive at ≥50 ng/mL; a negative result had a 99.5% negative predictive value for delivery within 1 week (Peaceman 1997, as cited by Ikeoha 2022); in one cohort (Mahomed 2019), birth within 7 days followed 1.8% of results <50 ng/mL and 16.1% of results ≥50 ng/mL. Token: valid sample — symptomatic, 24–34 weeks, membranes intact, no significant bleeding, cervix <3 cm, no intercourse in 24 h, swab before digital exam. MCA card: >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling with intrauterine transfusion (IUT) if anaemic; 100% sensitivity for moderate or severe anaemia with 12% false positives in Mari 2000; mild anaemia not predicted. Token: after 36 weeks and after previous transfusions, false results increase. Hook answers card.

cues.text: Fetal fibronectin is positive at fifty nanograms per millilitre or more. Its strength is the negative result: about ninety-nine and a half percent of women testing negative did not deliver within a week. In one cohort, a positive result was followed by birth within seven days in only about one in six.

The result is only valid on a proper sample: symptomatic women between twenty-four and thirty-four weeks, membranes intact, no significant bleeding, cervix under three centimetres, no intercourse in the previous day, and the swab taken before any digital examination.

A middle cerebral artery velocity above one and a half multiples of the median suggests moderate or severe anaemia and leads to fetal blood sampling, with transfusion if the fetus is anaemic. In a key study it caught every moderate or severe case with twelve percent false positives, but it did not predict mild anaemia. After thirty-six weeks, or after earlier transfusions, false results increase.

Back to the hook. The thirty-week lung test is unlikely to change management. The positive fibronectin raises risk but predicts delivery far less reliably than a negative result rules it out. The fast middle cerebral artery flow is the result that acts: refer for fetal blood sampling.

props.label: 24–34 wk · intact · < 3 cm · no sex 24 h · swab first
> 36 wk or after IUT: more false results

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Order an L/S ratio at 30 weeks to clear a scheduled delivery” (✓ gestational age dominates; at this age RDS risk stays high whatever the ratio, so the test rarely changes management); “Positive fFN = she will deliver this week” (✓ the negative result is the reliable one; a positive is a much weaker predictor, and in one cohort only 16.1% of positives delivered within 7 days); “MCA PSV >1.5 MoM detects all fetal anaemia” (✓ moderate or severe anaemia; mild anaemia was not predicted, and false results increase after 36 weeks or after transfusion).

cues.text: Trap one: order a lung maturity test at thirty weeks to clear a delivery. No: at that age the risk of respiratory distress stays high whatever the ratio, so the result rarely changes the plan.

Trap two: a positive fibronectin means she will deliver this week. No: the negative result is the reliable one. A positive is a much weaker predictor; in one cohort only about one in six delivered within seven days.

Trap three: a velocity above one and a half multiples of the median detects every fetal anaemia. No: it detects moderate or severe anaemia, misses mild anaemia, and gives more false results late in pregnancy or after transfusion.

props.title: ✗ “L/S at 30 weeks clears the delivery.”
lines: ✓ Gestational age dominates; rarely changes plan

props.title: ✗ “fFN positive = delivering this week.”
lines: ✓ Trust the negative; a positive is a weak predictor

scenes.title: Calendar, smoke alarm, speedometer
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The CALENDAR beats the lung ratio; fibronectin is a SMOKE ALARM — silence is reliable, the alarm is often false; the MCA is a SPEEDOMETER — thin, anaemic blood runs fast.” Tokens: calendar = L/S · smoke alarm = fFN · speedometer = MCA. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the calendar beats the lung ratio. Fibronectin is a smoke alarm: silence is reliable, but the alarm is often false. The middle cerebral artery is a speedometer: thin, anaemic blood runs fast.

Where it breaks: a mature lung test does not mean other organs are mature; a smoke alarm is useless on a bad sample, so the collection rules matter; and the speedometer misreads late in pregnancy and after transfusion, and does not register mild anaemia.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: MCA: errors > 36 wk / after IUT; mild missed

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “L/S ≥2.0 = mature, but gestational age dominates · trust a negative fFN (≥50 ng/mL positive, valid sample only)”, “MCA PSV >1.5 MoM → moderate or severe anaemia → fetal blood sampling”.

cues.text: Gestational age outweighs a mature lung ratio, a negative fetal fibronectin on a valid sample is the result to trust, and a middle cerebral artery velocity above one and a half multiples of the median flags moderate or severe fetal anaemia for fetal blood sampling.

props.label: L/S ≥ 2.0 but the calendar wins · trust a negative fFN
MCA PSV > 1.5 MoM → moderate/severe anaemia → fetal blood sampling

explanation.what: Plain language: three late-pregnancy questions get three different tests. Are the baby’s lungs ready? Measure surfactant lipids in amniotic fluid, but remember the calendar matters more. Is preterm birth about to happen? Swab for fetal fibronectin, the “glue” between membranes and uterus, and trust a negative result. Is the fetus anaemic? Measure how fast blood flows in a brain artery, because anaemic blood is thinner and is pumped harder. Scientific terms: surfactant, lecithin (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine), sphingomyelin, lecithin/sphingomyelin (L/S) ratio, phosphatidylglycerol (PG), lamellar body count (LBC), respiratory distress syndrome (RDS), fetal fibronectin (fFN), choriodecidual interface, negative predictive value, middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity (MCA PSV), multiple of the median (MoM), ΔOD450, intrauterine transfusion (IUT).
explanation.why: Lecithin rises late in gestation while sphingomyelin stays roughly constant, so the ratio climbs; but RDS risk depends strongly on gestational age, and other organs mature too. fFN normally fades from cervicovaginal fluid after about 24 weeks and reappears when the chorion separates from the decidua. In fetal anaemia, cardiac output rises and blood viscosity falls, so MCA velocity rises.
explanation.measure: L/S ≥2.0 (2:1) classic mature cutoff in non-diabetic pregnancies (one institution used 2.5, and 3.0 in diabetes); L/S is affected by blood and meconium, PG assays are not; LBC >50,000/µL suggests maturity, <15,000/µL immaturity. fFN positive at ≥50 ng/mL; valid in symptomatic women at 24–34 weeks with intact membranes, no significant bleeding, cervix <3 cm, no intercourse in 24 h, swab before digital exam; NPV for delivery within 1 week 99.5% (Peaceman 1997, as cited); in one cohort birth within 7 days followed 1.8% of <50 and 16.1% of ≥50 ng/mL results. MCA PSV >1.5 MoM: 100% sensitive for moderate or severe anaemia, 12% false positives, mild anaemia not predicted (Mari 2000); more false results after 36 weeks and after previous IUT.
explanation.differs: L/S (quantity ratio, blood/meconium sensitive) vs PG (not affected by blood/meconium); negative fFN (strong rule-out) vs positive fFN (weak rule-in); MCA Doppler (non-invasive, also used for anaemia not caused by haemolysis, such as Kell disease) vs amniotic ΔOD450 (invasive, reflects haemolysis only, misleads in Kell disease).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: the L/S cutoff for maturity, why FLM testing at 30 weeks or to justify elective early delivery is a poor choice, the meaning of a negative vs positive fFN and its sample rules, and the next step after MCA PSV >1.5 MoM.

Supports reassurance on a valid sample

right.label: Positive (≥ 50 ng/mL)

comparisons.distinguisher: fFN is a rule-out test: its negative result carries the weight.

comparisons.title: MCA Doppler vs amniotic ΔOD450
comparisons.distinguisher: Doppler measures the anaemic circulation directly; bilirubin measures haemolysis.

mnemonic.text: The CALENDAR beats the lung ratio; fibronectin is a SMOKE ALARM (silence is reliable, the alarm is often false); the MCA is a SPEEDOMETER (thin, anaemic blood runs fast).
mnemonic.explanation: Links each late-pregnancy test to its main interpretive rule.
mnemonic.limitation: A mature lung result does not mean other organs are mature; fFN is only valid on a properly collected sample; MCA PSV gives more false results after 36 weeks and after transfusion and does not detect mild anaemia.

analogyLimitations: Performance figures come from individual studies and differ between populations and assays.
takeaway: Gestational age outweighs a mature lung ratio, a negative fetal fibronectin on a valid sample is the result to trust, and a middle cerebral artery velocity above one and a half multiples of the median flags moderate or severe fetal anaemia for fetal blood sampling.

questions.stem: At 30 weeks, an obstetrician plans a scheduled delivery and sends amniotic fluid for an L/S ratio “to confirm the lungs are ready.” Which statement is best supported?

options.text: At this gestational age the risk of RDS stays high even with a mature-range ratio, so the result is unlikely to change management
options.rationale: Correct. In one cohort model no L/S value brought RDS risk to 3% or less before 34 weeks; gestational age dominates.

options.text: An L/S of 2.0 or more guarantees the neonate will have no complications
options.rationale: Incorrect. Neonates born before 39 weeks after a mature test still had substantial morbidity; lungs are not the only immature organ.

options.text: Blood contamination does not affect the L/S ratio
options.rationale: Incorrect. Blood and meconium can affect the L/S ratio; PG assays are the ones not affected.

options.text: Sphingomyelin rising above lecithin indicates maturity
options.rationale: Incorrect. Sphingomyelin exceeds lecithin until about 26 weeks; maturity is shown by lecithin rising to about twice sphingomyelin.

questions.stem: A woman at 29 weeks with contractions and intact membranes has a cervicovaginal fetal fibronectin of 80 ng/mL on a properly collected swab. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Her risk of preterm birth is increased, but a positive result predicts delivery far less reliably than a negative result rules it out
options.rationale: Correct. A positive (≥50 ng/mL) result raises risk, but positive predictive values vary widely between studies; in one cohort only 16.1% of positives delivered within 7 days. The negative result is the strong one.

options.text: Delivery within 7 days is essentially certain
options.rationale: Incorrect. fFN is a rule-out test; a positive result has a low positive predictive value.

options.text: The result is invalid because fFN can only be tested after 35 weeks
options.rationale: Incorrect. The test is used at 24–34 weeks; fFN is normally present in cervicovaginal fluid before 24 weeks, which is why testing starts at 24 weeks.

options.text: The result would still be valid if she had intercourse 6 hours before the swab
options.rationale: Incorrect. Intercourse within 24 hours excludes the sample; seminal fluid can affect fFN results.

questions.stem: In an anti-D alloimmunised pregnancy at 28 weeks with no previous transfusion, the MCA peak systolic velocity is 1.7 MoM. What is the best next step?

options.text: Refer for fetal blood sampling, with intrauterine transfusion if the fetus is anaemic
options.rationale: Correct. Above 1.5 MoM suggests moderate or severe anaemia, and fetal blood sampling confirms it before transfusion.

options.text: Reassure: 1.7 MoM is within normal limits
options.rationale: Incorrect. Above 1.5 MoM is the threshold used to flag moderate or severe anaemia (Mari 2000; used as the indication for transfusion in Pasman 2015).

options.text: Perform serial amniocentesis for ΔOD450 instead, because it is more sensitive
options.rationale: Incorrect. In the DIAMOND study MCA Doppler was more sensitive for severe anaemia (88% vs 76%), and amniocentesis carries loss and haemorrhage risks.

options.text: Conclude the fetus has mild anaemia only, because MCA detects all degrees of anaemia equally
options.rationale: Incorrect. MCA PSV did not predict mild anaemia; a value above 1.5 MoM points to moderate or severe anaemia.

references.citation: Peppiatt I, Retrouvey M, Conran RM. Educational Case: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome. Acad Pathol. 2024;11(2):100115. doi:10.1016/j.acpath.2024.100115
references.usedFor: Surfactant composition (lecithin/DPPC, PG); sphingomyelin exceeds lecithin until 26 weeks; L/S 2:1 = mature; L/S affected by blood/meconium, PG assays not; LBC >50,000/µL mature, <15,000/µL immature; FLM testing has decreased as ACOG and NICHD set stricter indications for late-preterm and early-term birth; antenatal corticosteroids decrease the need; surfactant does not indicate maturity of other organs.

references.citation: St Clair C, Norwitz ER, Woensdregt K, Cackovic M, Shaw JA, Malkus H, Ehrenkranz RA, Illuzzi JL. The probability of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome as a function of gestational age and lecithin/sphingomyelin ratio. Am J Perinatol. 2008;25(8):473-480. doi:10.1055/s-0028-1085066
references.usedFor: Read via a page-fetch tool (Europe PMC full text was empty). L/S 2.0 (or 2.5) long regarded as the maturity cutoff; institution used 2.5 non-diabetic and 3.0 diabetic; below 34 weeks no L/S value gave ≤3% RDS probability; at 26 weeks 97–99% regardless of L/S; gestational-age-specific cutoffs; wide confidence intervals (8 RDS cases).

references.citation: Wijnberger LD, de Kleine M, Voorbij HA, Arabin B, Bruinse HW, Visser GH, Bossuyt PM, Mol BW. Prediction of fetal lung immaturity using gestational age, patient characteristics and fetal lung maturity tests: a probabilistic approach. Arch Gynecol Obstet. 2010;281(1):15-21. doi:10.1007/s00404-009-1033-0
references.usedFor: L/S and LBC are invasive tests used when preterm delivery is at risk; both vary with gestational age; cites the view that testing is not useful before 32–33 weeks (high immaturity risk) or near term.

references.citation: Vanderhoeven JP, Peterson SE, Gannon EE, Mayock DE, Gammill HS. Neonatal morbidity occurs despite pulmonary maturity prior to 39 weeks gestation. J Perinatol. 2014;34(4):322-325. doi:10.1038/jp.2013.173
references.usedFor: Composite neonatal morbidity 32.4% in the mature FLM group before 39 weeks; FLM status did not correlate with the spectrum of neonatal morbidity; cites evidence that outcomes differ between neonates born before 39 weeks with mature testing and those born after 39 weeks; after adjustment, RDS (but not the composite outcome) remained more frequent in the immature/transitional group.

references.citation: Cao Z, Liu J, Xie X, Zhan S, Song W, Wu S, Sun Z, Dong Y, Tang G, Liu Y, Li L, Shen M, Zhai Y, Zou J, Liu X. Lipidomic profiling of amniotic fluid and its application in fetal lung maturity prediction. J Clin Lab Anal. 2020;34(4):e23109. doi:10.1002/jcla.23109
references.usedFor: L/S rises with gestation because sphingomyelin stays roughly constant while lecithin increases; PG is the last lipid to increase and is not affected by blood or meconium; conventional FLM methods (L/S by TLC, PG, S/A, LBC); S/A assay discontinued in 2011.

references.citation: Ikeoha CC, Anikwe CC, Umeononihu OS, Okorochukwu BC, Mamah JE, Eleje GU, et al. Fetal Fibronectin as a Predictor of Preterm Delivery: A Nigerian Cohort Study. Biomed Res Int. 2022;2022:2442338. doi:10.1155/2022/2442338
references.usedFor: fFN as an extracellular-matrix component at the choriodecidual junction; elevated in the first 24 weeks and diminishing between 24 and 34 weeks in normal pregnancy; Peaceman 1997 NPV 99.5% for delivery within 1 week and PPV 62.5% (cited, not read directly; PPV is reported very differently across studies); exclusion of intercourse/lubricant within 24 h, ruptured membranes, bleeding; dilation ≤3 cm.

references.citation: Chen CY, Chang CC, Yu C, Lin CW. Clinical application of surface plasmon resonance-based biosensors for fetal fibronectin detection. Sensors (Basel). 2012;12(4):3879-3890. doi:10.3390/s120403879
references.usedFor: fFN is a glycoprotein of the amniotic-membrane extracellular matrix; ≥50 ng/mL defined as positive; only about 1% of women with a negative result deliver within the next week; release by choriodecidual separation or inflammation; exclusions (dilation ≥3 cm, ruptured membranes, significant bleeding, intercourse within 24 h) and why.

references.citation: Mahomed K, Ibiebele I, Fraser C, Brown C. Predictive value of the quantitative fetal fibronectin levels for the management of women presenting with threatened preterm labour - A revised cut off level: A retrospective cohort study. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol X. 2019;4:100079. doi:10.1016/j.eurox.2019.100079
references.usedFor: Birth within 7 days after fFN <50 ng/mL 1.8% vs ≥50 ng/mL 16.1%; high NPV; fFN not normally done with ruptured membranes, vaginal bleeding, intercourse within 24 h, dilation ≥3 cm or cerclage; >70% of women with threatened preterm labour deliver at term.

references.citation: Peterson WE, Sprague AE, Reszel J, Walker M, Fell DB, Perkins SL, Dunn SI, Johnson M. Women's perspectives of the fetal fibronectin testing process: a qualitative descriptive study. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2014;14:190. doi:10.1186/1471-2393-14-190
references.usedFor: fFN absent at 24–34 weeks indicates a woman is unlikely to give birth within 7–14 days; vaginal swab must precede a digital examination for dilatation.

references.citation: Di Renzo GC, Roura LC, Facchinetti F, Antsaklis A, Breborowicz G, Gratacos E, et al. Guidelines for the management of spontaneous preterm labor: identification of spontaneous preterm labor, diagnosis of preterm premature rupture of membranes, and preventive tools for preterm birth. J Matern Fetal Neonatal Med. 2011;24(5):659-667. doi:10.3109/14767058.2011.553694
references.usedFor: Negative fFN identifies patients at very low risk; positive fFN associated with preterm delivery; Actim Partus is not affected by seminal fluid, unlike fFN (so fFN is unsuitable after recent intercourse).

references.citation: Brennand J. Middle cerebral artery Doppler. Australas J Ultrasound Med. 2009;12(3):35-38. doi:10.1002/j.2205-0140.2009.tb00058.x
references.usedFor: Physiology (higher cardiac output, lower viscosity → higher MCA PSV); MoM definition; Mari 2000: 100% sensitivity for moderate or severe anaemia, 12% false positives, mild anaemia not predicted, >1.5 MoM would have avoided 70% of invasive tests; higher false positives after intrauterine transfusion; ΔOD450 reflects haemolysis and misleads in Kell disease; amniocentesis loss 0.25–1% and fetomaternal haemorrhage 2.3–17%; DIAMOND sensitivity 88% (MCA) vs 76% (amniocentesis) for severe anaemia.

references.citation: Pasman SA, Claes L, Lewi L, Van Schoubroeck D, Debeer A, Emonds M, Geuten E, De Catte L, Devlieger R. Intrauterine transfusion for fetal anemia due to red blood cell alloimmunization: 14 years experience in Leuven. Facts Views Vis Obgyn. 2015;7(2):129-136.
references.usedFor: MCA PSV replaced amniocentesis ΔOD450 for timing transfusion and quickly became standard; MCA PSV >1.5 MoM used as indication for IUT/fetal blood sampling; after 36 weeks MCA PSV more often false positive or negative.

claims.text: Surfactant lipids; sphingomyelin > lecithin until ~26 weeks; L/S ≥2.0 mature; L/S affected by blood/meconium, PG not; LBC thresholds.
Gestational age dominates RDS risk: below 34 weeks no L/S gave ≤3% risk; 26 weeks 97–99% regardless; testing at low gestation rarely changes management.
Mature FLM before 39 weeks does not prevent substantial neonatal morbidity; FLM testing has declined with stricter indications and routine antenatal steroids.
fFN is a choriodecidual glycoprotein, present before 24 weeks, normally diminishing at 24–34 weeks, released with choriodecidual separation.
fFN positive at ≥50 ng/mL; NPV 99.5% within 1 week (Peaceman 1997 as cited); birth within 7 days 1.8% (<50) vs 16.1% (≥50) in one cohort.
claims.note: Peaceman 1997 was not read directly; its NPV is taken from Ikeoha 2022 and is consistent with Chen 2012 (about 1% of negatives deliver within a week).

claims.text: Valid sample: symptomatic, 24–34 weeks, intact membranes, no significant bleeding, cervix <3 cm, no intercourse in 24 h, swab before digital exam.
Fetal anaemia raises cardiac output and lowers viscosity, raising MCA PSV; MoM = measured ÷ expected for gestational age.
MCA PSV >1.5 MoM: 100% sensitivity for moderate/severe anaemia, 12% false positives, mild not predicted; leads to fetal blood sampling/IUT; more false results after 36 weeks and after IUT.
MCA Doppler replaced amniocentesis ΔOD450; ΔOD450 reflects haemolysis only (misleads in Kell); amniocentesis loss 0.25–1%, FMH 2.3–17%; DIAMOND 88% vs 76%.
Reviewer’s “PG appears after ~35 weeks”; hard “not useful before 32 weeks” cutoff; fFN window “24–35 weeks”; ACOG committee opinion wording; Queenan curve.
claims.note: Not taught as stated. No open source read gave PG timing; the StatPearls L/S chapter was blocked by browser verification; the ACOG document itself was not read.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 26 Hit 8 says “Don’t deliver <39 weeks without confirming [lung maturity] unless dates are certain,” implying a mature FLM test justifies earlier delivery. Vanderhoeven 2014 found substantial neonatal morbidity before 39 weeks despite mature FLM results, and Peppiatt 2024 reports that FLM testing has declined as ACOG and NICHD adopted stricter indications for late-preterm and early-term birth (register flag rv-flm-mature-before-39-weeks).

Ch. 26 Hit 11 says MCA PSV >1.5 MoM “detects all fetal anemia (12% false-positive).” In Mari 2000 (summarised by Brennand 2009) sensitivity was 100% for moderate or severe anaemia and mild anaemia was not predicted; DIAMOND reported 88% sensitivity for severe anaemia, and false results increase after 36 weeks and after transfusion (register flag rv-mca-psv-moderate-severe-only).
